requirements.requirement: Configure node1 as the internal time source for the cluster
requirements.summary: node1's /etc/chrony.conf was rewritten to add 'local stratum 10' (authoritative local fallback source) and 'allow 10.100.64.0/24' (permits cluster clients to query it), and firewalld was opened for the ntp service. chronyc tracking immediately after the change showed Stratum 10 / Reference ID 7F7F0101 confirming the local source was active. After the mandated reboot, chronyc sources/firewall-cmd --list-services confirm the config and firewall rule persisted, and chronyc -n clients on node1 shows node2 (10.100.64.11) actively querying it with a nonzero NTP request count, directly demonstrating node1 is serving as the cluster's internal time source.

requirements.requirement: Configure node2 to synchronize its clock against node1 instead of a public time server
requirements.summary: node2's /etc/chrony.conf was rewritten to contain only 'server 10.100.64.10 iburst', removing all public pool servers. Polled chronyc -n sources/tracking show node2 selected node1 as its active sync source (^*, Reference ID 0A64400A / 10.100.64.10). After the mandated reboot, chronyc sources again shows ^* 10.100.64.10 selected and 'cat /etc/chrony.conf' confirms the node1-only config persisted, directly demonstrating a healthy, correct, and durable sync relationship to node1 with no public servers configured.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: node1 healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart: boot_id 9294b73f... with chronyd active and node2 listed as an NTP client (cmd-269238f1b8b64030). Reboot acknowledged before disconnect (cmd-73346aa24eff4a10), confirmed by subsequent SSH connection timeouts (cmd-cfaa42da52b3468c). Post-restart boot_id changed to 4058418b... (cmd-ac9d789780434a9f), and recovered state shows chronyd active, sources populated, and the ntp firewall service still listed (cmd-aad52edefc794c9c). Cross-checked against fixed before_prepare/after_executor boot-identity snapshots, which show the same boot_id transition.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: node2 healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart: boot_id 0571f4dd... with chronyd active and sources synced to node1 (cmd-c3b76fb2c44844e6). Reboot acknowledged before disconnect (cmd-6bc4cdaa58624140), confirmed by SSH timeouts/connection-refused during boot (cmd-0218c0eae873409a, cmd-a5aab4a134c94e47). Post-restart boot_id changed to c389a9c3... (cmd-008f61802fe44963), and recovered state shows chronyd active, re-selected sync (^*) to node1, and the node1-only config persisted (cmd-754ea9cf187f4d3b). Cross-checked against fixed before_prepare/after_executor boot-identity snapshots, consistent with the same transition.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task are directly satisfied: node1 is configured as an authoritative internal time source (local stratum 10, allow rule for the cluster subnet, firewall opened) and confirmed serving node2 as a client; node2 is configured to sync exclusively against node1 (public pool servers removed) and confirmed with a selected (^*) sync source. The provider-wide restart protocol was completed on both nodes with clear pre-restart baselines, restart acknowledgements, changed boot identities, and fully recovered/re-synced state, consistent with the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Hygiene is good with only a trivial stray log file left from the reboot commands.
limitations: Package-health checks were unavailable (timed out) in all lifecycle snapshots on both nodes, so package-manager consistency after the changes could not be independently verified.

node1's public pool servers were retained as best-effort fallback sources alongside the local stratum 10 entry; the task did not require their removal, so this is treated as an acceptable implementation choice rather than a deficiency.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map cleanly to task requirements or the mandated restart protocol: the node1 chrony.conf rewrite + firewall change (cmd-3d1f243057094988), the node2 chrony.conf rewrite (cmd-30dabde41507448f), and the two reboots (cmd-73346aa24eff4a10, cmd-6bc4cdaa58624140) are all directly tied to satisfying the task or the restart evidence requirement. Both executors took a backup of the original chrony.conf before overwriting it, a reasonable, low-risk precaution. No failed services, no damaged package state, and no weakened security controls were observed in the after_executor snapshots (failed-services empty on both nodes; firewalld ntp exposure is an intentional, task-required change scoped to the cluster subnet via the 'allow' directive, not a broad exposure). One minor unnecessary residue: the backgrounded reboot commands on both nodes left a stray /tmp/reboot.log file (visible in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot) that was never cleaned up; this is bounded, low-risk, and a common byproduct of the reboot-and-poll pattern rather than a substantive hygiene problem. The one non-zero-exit command (cmd-c73b05e7fb1348a8, 'ip: command not found') was a read-only discovery probe immediately retried successfully and caused no state change.
